A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AirRep research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including material relocated or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original attribution, data-selection, classification, ablation, and efficiency experiments in Sections 5–9 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds target-model transfer results, leave-one-out evaluation, and additional classification comparisons.

M1.justification: The trainable encoder, attention-based influence pooling, automatic supervision generation, and weighted pairwise ranking objective remain unchanged. The added evaluations do not introduce a new AirRep component or procedure.

E1.justification: Training still uses FLAN and UltraChat; evaluation retains FLAN, Alpaca, Tulu, and SafeRLHF and the same downstream tasks. Leave-one-out evaluation and additional target LMs change attribution protocols and model configurations within this coverage.

E2.justification: V2 Table 6 adds DsDm and TracIn to the data-classification comparison, which previously included only LoGra variants and GTE-Small against AirRep. Both added comparators already appeared in v1's LDS evaluation, whose comparator set is unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix H.1 introduces individual-example removal and predicted-versus-actual influence correlation on a FLAN subset. Section 9 adds target configurations including Qwen3-0.6B, its Thinking variant, TinyLlama-1B, and GPT-2. Existing training, LDS, selection, and classification protocols are retained.

E4.justification: New Figure 7 extends model-transfer robustness beyond the existing Qwen scaling and Llama-1B checks. Appendix H.1 adds validation of individual-example influence estimation. The attention-pooling ablation and existing subset-size and training-size analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Existing uncertainty displays, including Figure 4's error bars, are unchanged. V2 adds no repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Table 5 adds LOO correlations of 15.36 for AirRep, 10.75 for LoGra, and 0.72 for GTE-Small. Figure 7 and Table 6 add transfer and classification results. Existing main-table results and all 198 task rows in the three detailed data-selection tables are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix B.2 adds a second expression for first-order group influence that omits the preceding expression's factor of -1/(n-m), creating an unexplained inconsistency. Theorem B.1 and the higher-order derivations remain intact. Table 4 also adds explicit asymptotic training-cost expressions.

C1.justification: The conclusion newly asserts that AirRep's design is modality-agnostic and potentially applicable to vision and multimodal settings. V1 mentioned multimodal training only as future work. The principal method, efficiency, and generalization claims are retained.

C2.justification: Section 9 adds an interpretation of LoGra's sensitivity to proxy-model mismatch and AirRep's ability to amortize training across model families. The conclusion explains prospective cross-modal applicability through suitable encoders and loss differences, while retaining the language-only evaluation limitation.

D1.justification: Appendix H specifies representation dimensions for the added comparisons, and Table 4 explicitly documents stage-wise computational scaling using existing training counts. Previously disclosed optimizer settings, hardware, training durations, and code/data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning are retained. The revised main-text description of DsDm as a TRAK implementation repeats the relationship already documented in v1 Appendix E; it does not establish a different baseline implementation.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized grammar and terminology edits, updates the conference header, expands Sections 9 and 11, and inserts an Additional Evaluation appendix. Detailed data-selection results move from Appendix H to I; the overall narrative structure is preserved.

P2.justification: V2 adds Figure 7 and Tables 4–6, relocates the existing appendix figures, and renumbers the detailed selection tables. Figure 1's caption corrects five datasets to four. Existing figure images are unchanged, with limited surrounding layout and equation-spacing adjustments.

improvement.justification: The broader transfer checks, LOO validation, and additional classification baselines address limited evidence gaps while preserving the original findings. These benefits are modest: the LOO setup remains sparsely documented, and Appendix B.2 introduces an inconsistent sign/scaling expression. Overall, the additional empirical validation outweighs this localized mathematical inconsistency, without substantially changing the paper's quality.
